newsitem.title: USA: Turner officials could reap rich options.
newsitem.headline: Turner officials could reap rich options.

text.p: Turner Broadcasting System Inc executive vice president Terence McGuirk and seven other company executives would become eligible for severance packages worth $28.3 million with the likely merger of Time Warner and Turner.
The year-old merger agreement, now valued at $6.5 billion, is widely expected to be approved Oct. 10, when shareholders of Time Warner and Turner meet separately in New York City.
Closing the deal constitutes a breach in each executive's contract and could spur the payments if the eight do not sign on with the new company, according to a proxy on the merger.
The roles of the executives, if any, in the combined Time Warner-Turner have not been made public.
Turner chairman and chief executive Ted Turner is not among the eight. He is scheduled to become vice chairman of the new company and an equity owner with shares worth about $2 billion.

According to the proxy, Ted Turner will be entitled to substantial stock options over the next five years and an annual salary of $1.05 million. One compensation expert valued the options at $21.8 million, according to the Wall Street Journal.

The proxy also said three top executives at the New Line and Castle Rock movie studios owned by Turner Broadcasting will become eligible to convert Turner options into Time Warner options with a value of $51 million as of June 30.
